newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power mostly lower, seen near normal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power mostly lower, seen near normal.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West eased Tuesday to what traders saw as near-normal levels for early November, with mild weather and generating units returning from outages, sources said. "Prices are falling, but the levels we're seeing now are closer to what you'd expect for this time of year," said one Mid-West marketer.

Several generating units were reported to be returning to service, including TVA Nuclear's 1,148 megawatt Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Tennessee, and Commonwealth Edison's 789 megawatt Quad Cities nuclear power unit 2 in Illinois. Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) were talked steady to higher for Wednesday delivery at $18.00-21.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $17.00-19.00 in Monday discussion, the brokers and marketers said.

Off-peak next-day ECAR power was assessed little changed at $12.50-14.00 for Wednesday delivery. Peak ECAR power for December was pegged relatively steady to slightly higher at $19.40-19.80 from $19.35-19.75 in Monday discussion, the sources said.

January/February was talked steady at $21.40-21.80. In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power for Wednesday delivery was talked steady at $17.00-19.00 per MWh, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was said to have held steady at $9.00-10.00 per MWh.

In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power for Wednesday was talked lower at $21.00-22.00 in the north area from $21.00-24.00 on Monday, while prices were assessed at $19.00-20.00 in the south from $19.00-21.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Off-peak next day MAIN power was pegged steady at $12.00-14.00 per MWh.

Peak non-firm next-day power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) were talked at $21.50-21.80, down from next-day pricing of $23.00-26.00 in the north and $21.00-22.50 in the south on Monday, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were reported to be steady
Peak December SPP power was said to be talked higher at
$22.60-22.90 from $21.85-22.05 on Monday, the sources said. -- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627 REUTER
